fields.meta_title: Slider Scale Survey Builder With Custom Ranges | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Create a slider scale survey with your own range, step and end labels. See the average for each question and keep every score in a database.
fields.h1: Build a Slider Scale Survey With Your Own Range and Labels
fields.hero_description: Build a slider scale survey people answer with one drag, and save each answer as a number in your own database.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Slider Survey
fields.features_subheading: Each answer on a slider is a number. Emergent builds the track people drag and the table that adds those numbers up.
fields.feature_1:
Range, step, and end labels you set

Tell Emergent the range and the step, such as 0 to 100 in steps of 5, and the words at each end. The slider snaps to those points, and a later prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_2:
A handle that waits to be moved

Ask for a handle that stays hidden until someone taps the track, so no answer starts at a default value. A slider nobody touched saves as blank, never as a quiet score of 50.
fields.feature_3:
One slider per screen on a phone

Respondents see one question per screen and drag with a thumb, with the current value shown above the handle. The same survey opens on a laptop with the same steps and labels.
fields.feature_4:
Each score kept as a plain number

Each answer lands as a number in its own column of a database you own, with the question and the time it arrived. Set this quarter's average beside last quarter's without retyping.
fields.feature_5:
Averages and a low-score alert

The dashboard shows the average, the median, and the spread of scores for each slider. Set a floor, and the app sends an email or a Slack message when an average falls below it.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Every survey Emergent builds is code. On paid plans, export it to your GitHub repository with the slider settings, the scoring and the dashboard, and run the next round from there.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Teams Measuring on a Slider
fields.tab_content_1:
Android trails iOS by 19 points on export

Lindqvale, a photo editing app, asks 520 users to rate its new export screen on a slider of 0 to 100. The overall average of 70 hides a split. The 300 iOS users average 78, the 220 on Android average 59, and the team opens a bug review for the Android export flow.
fields.tab_content_2:
A team average under 5 emails its manager

Every Friday, Pebblecroft Freight asks each employee one question on a 0 to 10 slider: how manageable was this week's workload? When a team's average falls below 5, the app emails that team's manager. This week the 18 people on support averaged 4.2, and their manager saw it before Monday.
fields.tab_content_3:
Confidence climbs 3.5 points in one workshop

Before the workshop starts, Wrexley Community College asks 64 attendees to rate their spreadsheet confidence on a 1 to 10 slider, one question per screen on their phones. The same slider opens again at the end. The class average moves from 3.9 to 7.4, and the college keeps the session on next term's schedule.
fields.tab_content_4:
With a $40 ceiling, subscribers settle on $12

Dovecote Pantry wants a price for a breakfast add-on to its meal kits. It asks 312 subscribers what they would pay each month on a slider of $0 to $40 in $1 steps. The median answer is $12, and 128 answers fall between $10 and $15. The team launches the add-on at $12.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Slider Scale Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a slider scale survey with a range and labels people read the same way, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the range and the step
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one thing each slider measures, such as effort on a new screen or confidence with spreadsheets, and the words for each end. If an end label needs a full sentence, the slider is measuring two things. Split it into two questions.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use 0 to 10 when people answer on gut feeling, and 0 to 100 when small differences matter, such as a before-and-after score. Set the step as well. A step of 5 on a 0 to 100 slider gives 21 points to land on.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Label both ends in words, and the midpoint too when the scale has a neutral center. Keep each label short enough to sit under the track on a phone, such as Not at all and Completely. Use the same labels on every slider that measures the same thing.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Start the handle hidden, or at the left end, rather than in the middle. A handle resting at 50 lets someone submit 50 without touching it. Ask for an untouched slider to save as blank, and skipped questions show up as gaps, not as scores.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent the questions, the range, the step, the end labels, and where the handle starts, in plain sentences. Emergent builds the survey, the database table behind it, and the dashboard. Change any of those settings later with another prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it on a phone with five people
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the survey to five people and watch them answer on their phones. Check that the handle is easy to grab, that the value shows while they drag, and that each answer lands in the table as the exact number they picked.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the median and the spread next to the average. An average of 50 can mean everyone sat near the middle, or that half the group said 10 and half said 90. Split the results by the field that matters, such as platform or team.

faq_plan.q: What is a good 5-point rating scale for a survey?
faq_plan.ref: What is a good 5-point rating scale for a survey?

prov.original: What is a good 5-point rating scale for a survey?

faq_plan.a: A good 5-point scale is balanced and labeled at every point: Very dissatisfied, Dissatisfied, Neither satisfied nor dissatisfied, Satisfied, and Very satisfied. Its positive and negative options match in number, and the odd number of points gives a neutral midpoint. When five steps feel too coarse, a slider scale survey of 0 to 100 gives people room between them.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a slider scale survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in Emergent's AI survey builder: what each slider asks, its range and step, the words at either end, and whether the handle stays hidden until tapped. Emergent builds the survey and a results dashboard from that prompt, with a database table behind them. Try it with a few people on their phones, then adjust any setting with a follow-up prompt.

faq_plan.q: Is a slider better than buttons in a rating scale survey?
faq_plan.a: Not always. Buttons suit a rating scale survey with five or seven labeled points, where each point has a clear meaning. A slider suits finer steps, such as 0 to 100, or small changes you plan to compare over time. Try both on a phone before you choose.

faq_plan.q: What can a slider scale survey measure besides satisfaction?
faq_plan.a: A slider measures any amount that runs between two ends, such as confidence or the price someone would pay. An onboarding survey can ask new hires to score how ready they feel out of 10 after week one and again after a month. The survey Emergent builds keeps every score in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What range should a slider scale survey use?
faq_plan.a: Use 0 to 10 for quick ratings and 0 to 100 when you want finer steps or plan to compare scores before and after a change. SurveyMonkey's slider question defaults to a range of 0 to 100. Keep one range across every slider in a survey, and scores compare directly.

faq_plan.q: Should the handle in a slider scale survey start in the middle?
faq_plan.a: No. Hide it until someone taps the track, or start it at the left end. SurveyMonkey handles untouched sliders the same way: respondents need to take action on the question in order to record a response for it. A blank is easier to read in results than a default value nobody chose.

faq_plan.q: How do I analyze slider scale survey results?
faq_plan.a: Check how the scores cluster before you trust the average, then split them by the fields you collected, such as platform or team. A brand perception survey on 0 to 100 sliders can show one group at 80 and another at 40 behind an average of 60. Emergent builds those splits into the dashboard from your prompt.

faq_plan.q: Does the top of the range change slider scale survey answers?
faq_plan.a: It can. In a YouGov experiment, ceiling values exhibit anchor effects by altering the mean price reported. Set the top of a price slider at a real upper limit, not a round number picked for looks.

faq_plan.q: Does a slider scale survey work well on a phone?
faq_plan.a: It does when the track is wide and the handle is big enough for a thumb. Put one slider on each screen, show the value above the handle while people drag, and keep end labels to two or three words. Emergent builds conversational surveys that show one question per screen.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a slider scale survey have?
faq_plan.a: Three or four sliders suit a recurring check-in that people answer in about a minute. A weekly mental health survey, for example, can ask about mood and sleep on 0 to 10 sliders, with one open comment box. A longer one-off survey can carry more, grouped into sections of five or six sliders.
